picks.rationale: Sunderland is playing their first European home game in 53 years, which should provide a significant motivational boost and home-field advantage. Historically, AZ Alkmaar has a very poor record when playing in England in UEFA competitions, having lost all 11 of their previous clashes. Sunderland has no new injury concerns, while AZ Alkmaar is missing Kees Smit due to injury. This combination of home advantage, historical trend, and injury status strongly favors Sunderland.

Lyon holds a strong head-to-head advantage over Anderlecht, having won three of their four prior meetings. Anderlecht also struggles against French opposition, with only one win in their last eleven games against teams from France. Furthermore, Anderlecht is significantly hampered by several key defensive injuries, including Giulian Biancone, Lucas Hey, Ilay Camara, and Killian Sardella. Lyon is in solid recent form, being unbeaten in Ligue 1 and on a three-match unbeaten run since their Champions League exit.

The head-to-head history between Dinamo Zagreb and Hapoel Be'er Sheva strongly indicates a high-scoring affair, with both of their previous encounters exceeding 1.5, 2.5, and even 3.5 goals. Dinamo Zagreb has demonstrated good offensive capabilities, securing seven victories in their last twelve matches across all competitions. Hapoel Be'er Sheva has also shown an ability to find the back of the net, winning three of their last five home games. These factors suggest a high likelihood of at least three goals in this match.

Rennes enters this match in strong recent form, boasting three wins, one draw, and one loss in their last five outings. A key indicator of their strong performance is their tendency to start games aggressively, having scored first in all of their last five matches. While specific head-to-head or injury information for SK Sturm Graz was not available, Rennes' consistent ability to take early leads and their overall solid form provide a significant edge.
